title: Understanding Ridge vs. LASSO
text: Ridge regression and LASSO regression both add a penalty to the loss function to prevent overfitting. However, they differ in how they apply this penalty. Ridge regression uses an L2 penalty, which tends to shrink coefficients evenly, while LASSO uses an L1 penalty, which can shrink some coefficients to zero. How might this affect the model's complexity and bias?

title: Effect on Model Bias
text: Consider how reducing the number of features by setting some coefficients to zero (as LASSO does) might affect the model's ability to fit the training data. Would this increase or decrease the model's bias?

title: Comparing Bias
text: If LASSO regression reduces the number of features by setting some coefficients to zero, how does this affect the model's bias compared to Ridge regression?
